business_problem: Tampere wanted to explore generative AI safely and turn that learning into practical internal public-service use cases and governance rather than scattered experimentation.
solution_summary: Capgemini and Sogeti helped the City of Tampere turn early generative-AI interest into a governed internal service architecture rather than isolated experiments. The work combined AI governance design, learning circles across city functions, and two hands-on pilots built on the city's own information sources: Ask HR and Ask About Procurement Contracts. Instead of opening models against all internal content at once, Tampere deliberately scoped the first deployment to HR information on the city intranet, using GPT-based capabilities to support dialogue and retrieval while reducing risk. Capgemini also designed a reusable architecture so additional use cases could be added without rebuilding the foundation each time. That made the project both a live knowledge-access implementation and a framework for scaling future municipal AI services under shared governance, training, and change-management practices.

solution_components.name: Ask HR
solution_components.role: Provides an internal generative AI assistant for HR information and employee dialogue.

solution_components.name: Ask About Procurement Contracts
solution_components.role: Gives staff a targeted assistant for answering questions about procurement-contract information.

solution_components.name: GPT models
solution_components.role: Power the generative AI dialogue and retrieval capabilities inside the city's pilot assistants.

data_flow: Targeted internal information such as HR content and procurement-contract material is scoped into the pilot architecture, where GPT-based assistants interpret employee questions and return answers through Ask HR or Ask About Procurement Contracts. Governance and learning practices wrap the flow so new use cases can be added without reopening all city data at once.
business_outcome: Tampere gained live internal AI pilots, stronger AI governance, and a reusable architecture for scaling future municipal AI services without losing control over risk, learning, and change management.
